name: Crypto stress
summary: Binance reopening after record $6.3bn hack; Bitcoin 10% off its high
state: Binance, the largest exchange, began resuming withdrawals on 31 Oct after about $6.3bn was drained in late October, saying about 90% of stolen user assets are covered (CNBC). The FBI attributed the theft to North Korea on 1 Nov. Bitcoin was near $78,200 early on 2 Nov, about 10% below its high; the exchange's promised proof of reserves is the next marker.
for_you: Binance customers may still face delays on some withdrawals. Any shortfall in reserves would matter most for those holding funds on the exchange.
rubric_hit: Top-10 exchange under stress (Binance hack, phased withdrawals) = Watch; BTC drawdown 10% < 25%

sources.title: CNBC — Binance resumes withdrawals following $6.3 billion hack
NBC News — FBI says North Korea was behind the $6.3 billion Binance hack

assessor_note: Metric floor is green, but the rubric's Watch criterion 'top-10 exchange under stress' still applies while Binance restores withdrawals after the $6.3bn hack.
why: Crypto is now plumbed into mainstream finance via ETFs and stablecoins; a crash or de-peg can spill into funding markets.
drivers: Liquidity, leverage, regulation, stablecoin reserves, exchange solvency.

rubric.alert: Drawdown > 45%, or a major stablecoin de-pegs (> 3% for > 24h), or a top-10 exchange fails.
rubric.watch: Drawdown 25–45%, or a top-10 exchange/stablecoin under stress.
rubric.normal: Bitcoin drawdown from 52-week high < 25% and no major stablecoin/exchange incidents.
